newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish petrol price to include road tax - minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish petrol price to include road tax - minister.

text.p: Polish Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki said on Thursday he wanted to go ahead with a long-delayed plan to include the current road tax in the price of petrol despite protests from local governments.

"I expect a government decision on the issue, there is a chance it would be taken this year," Liberadzki told a news conference, adding that the new law could take effect on January 1, 1998, if parliament approves it.
He said the tax for car owners, known as the road tax and collected by local governments, was widely evaded.

Now the tax is levied on car owners depending on the size of their vehicles' by the local authorities, which are under no obligation to spend the tax revenue on the construction and maintenance of roads, which are in terrible shape, he added.
Liberadzki said he prepared two scenarios for the inclusion of the road tax in the petrol price.

Both would involve increasing the price of petrol, which now costs between 1.22 zloty (45 cents) and 1.62 zloty (60 cents) per litre depending on quality and type, by about four or seven groszes (three cents) per litre.
But the two plans assumed a different share-out of tax revenues between local authorities and the central budget responsible for the maintenance and construction of national roads.

An idea to include the road tax in the petrol price emerged three years ago but has been blocked by protests from local governments which feared a loss of a significant source of revenues and concerns that a one-off petrol price increase might boost inflation.

The transport ministry supports the new system saying it would make millions of foreigners visiting Poland on route to other destinations or crossing the borders to fill their tanks with cheaper petrol, share the cost of road maintenance.
